name: Centro Historico
description: The historic core around Praca Horacio de Matos and Rua das Pedras is where most visitors base themselves: cobbled streets lined with pastel 19th-century diamond-boom facades, small museums, cafes, tour agencies, and the town's main restaurants. Everything is walkable but hilly. It is the most convenient area for trekking logistics and evening socializing, though also the busiest and noisiest during peak season.
bestFor: first-time visitors, trekkers booking tours, short stays
pros: walk to everything including tour offices and restaurants
best selection of cafes and evening spots
cons: steep uneven cobblestones are tough on ankles and luggage
can feel crowded and noisy in peak season

name: Rio Lencois riverside
description: The area following the Rio Lencois as it runs through the edge of town offers a calmer, greener alternative to the packed center, with natural swimming spots, a slower pace, and a short walk into the historic core. Several pousadas here lean into garden and river views rather than central bustle, appealing to visitors who want easy nature access without leaving town.
bestFor: longer stays, travelers wanting a calmer base, swimming access
pros: quieter and greener than the center
still a short walk to restaurants and tours
cons: fewer dining options directly in the area
wifi tends to be weaker further from the center

name: Alto da Conquista
description: A residential, uphill area on the edge of the historic center where many family-run pousadas and small guesthouses cluster among local homes, offering views over the rooftops and surrounding hills. It trades some convenience for quiet and often better value than center-facing rooms, with the walk into town taking about ten to fifteen minutes over more cobblestones.
bestFor: budget-conscious stays, travelers wanting a more local feel
pros: good value pousadas with hill views
still close enough to walk into the center
cons: steep walk up and down to the center daily
fewer amenities within the area itself

name: Vale do Capao
description: A separate village roughly two hours from Lencois by road, Vale do Capao is a popular alternative base for exploring the southern and more remote parts of Chapada Diamantina, known for its alternative, artsy community, organic cafes, and direct access to trails like Cachoeirao and Gruta Azul. Many nomads split time between Lencois and Capao for a different pace and trail set.
bestFor: longer treks, a more bohemian community, exploring southern Chapada
pros: direct access to a different set of major trails
cons: about two hours from Lencois town, requiring a separate trip
even more limited connectivity and infrastructure
